'''Brandon Clarke''' (born September 19, 1996) is a Canadian [[basketball]] player. He played for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. He has declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gay |first1=Carlan |title=Canadian Brandon Clarke to forgo final season at Gonzaga and enter his name in the 2019 NBA Draft |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/canadian-brandon-clarke-forgo-final-season-gonzaga-enter-2019-nba-draft/ewz2ixqsu42i1aujr2o0odkz7 |accessdate=17 April 2019 |work=NBA.com |date=17 April 2019}}</ref>

==Early years==
Clarke was born in [[Vancouver]], [[British Columbia]], to a Canadian mother Whitney Triplett and a Jamaican father Steve Clarke. Brandon moved to the United States at the age of three, settling in [[Phoenix, Arizona]].<ref>{{cite web |title=West Coast Conference - Crumpacker: Brandon Clarke Bolstering Bulldogs |url=https://wccsports.com/news/2018/12/14/mens-basketball-crumpacker-brandon-clarke-bolstering-bulldogs.aspx.aspx |website=wccsports.com |accessdate=9 April 2019}}</ref> He attended [[Desert Vista High School]] in Phoenix.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Prehm |first1=Matt |title=Oregon makes final three for big-time basketball transfer |url=https://247sports.com/college/oregon/Bolt/Oregon-makes-final-three-for-big-time-basketball-transfer-106469710/ |accessdate=27 September 2018 |work=247Sports |date=August 24, 2017}}</ref> He was named All-Arizona Division 1 honoree by the [[Arizona Republic]] after leading Desert Vista to the championship game in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=SJSUSpartans.com - Brandon Clarke Bio - San Jose State University Official Athletic Site Men's Basketball |url=http://www.sjsuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/brandon_clarke_972548.html |website=SJSUSpartans.com |accessdate=27 September 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
He played two seasons for the [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State Spartans]]. As a freshman he was named [[Mountain West]] Six Man of the Year by the league's head coaches after putting up 10.1 points and 7.3 rebounds in conference play.

As a sophomore, he averaged 17.3 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.6 blocks, and 2.3 assists on route to being named All-Mountain West First Team and Mountain West All-Defensive Team. After the season he decided to transfer to Gonzaga, where he redshirted the 2017-18 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brandon Clarke -2017-18 Men's Basketball Roster - Gonzaga University |url=https://gozags.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=326 |website=GoZags |accessdate=27 September 2018}}</ref>

In his junior season at Gonzaga, Clarke continued onward with his improvements to be named the [[West Coast Conference]]'s Newcomer of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, and be named a member of the All-WCC First Team. Clarke was the first player in WCC history to win both their Newcomer of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year honors in the same season.<ref>{{cite press release|title=WCC Announces 2018-19 Men’s Basketball All-Conference Team|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2019/3/5/wcc-announces-2018-19-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx|accessdate=March 5, 2019|publisher=West Coast Conference |date=March 5, 2019}}</ref> He was also named to the All-American Third Team by the [[Sporting News]]. On March 23, 2019, Clarke recorded a career-high 36 points alongside 8 rebounds, 5 blocks, and 3 assists in a 83–71 win over #9 seeded [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]]. He became the third player in NCAA Tournament history to record a game of 35+ points alongside 5 blocks, joining both [[Shaquille O'Neal]] and [[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]] as the only players to do that.<ref>https://twitter.com/JeffFaraudo/status/1109628490096078849</ref> Clarke also broke a team record in points scored in an NCAA Tournament, breaking a record previously set by [[Adam Morrison]].<ref>https://twitter.com/marchmadness/status/1109628219098099712</ref>
